title: Cross-venue perpetual basis (OKX vs Binance)
data_horizon: ~17 hours of overlapping marks between OKX and Binance

structural_finding.interpretation: Largest observed basis (5 bps) is 6.25% of the round-trip cost (80 bps). The p99 of the basis (3 bps) is 3.75% of the cost. The signal does not fire at any threshold that would net positive.

verdict.reason: too few trades: 0 < 30 (no complete walk-forward windows — 17h of data, 1440 bars, walk-forward needs >=455 daily bars)

data_caveat: OKX public 'history-mark-price-candles' endpoint is mislabeled — verified via 50-page probe: it returns the same 24h rolling window regardless of the 'after' cursor. This is the same hard 24-100 day cap your prior workspace hit on Coinbase hourly (~300d) and OKX funding (~100d). The walk-forward cannot be evaluated because the data is too short to form even one chained test window.
verdict: INSUFFICIENT DATA + STRUCTURAL FAILURE. Same finding as round 4.2: cross-venue mark-price basis is far smaller than retail cost schedule. Same data-availability wall as rounds 1-8.
next_action: loop policy says pick the next input class. Round 10 was 1-minute microstructure, but it has the same public-data cap. Honest move: write a SYNTHESIS log and stop the loop with the structural finding, rather than continue producing 'INSUFFICIENT DATA' verdicts.
